headline_signal: All four GMs voted trial. None subscribed. None passed. The site has methodological credibility but no persona felt the published work was actionable enough to commit budget.

article_scoreboard.verdict: unanimous best — the only finding any persona said they'd hand to their analytics group on Monday
solid methodology but every persona flagged the max_fv=0 instrument coverage problem as undermining the headline
interesting framing but no persona said it would change a trade decision
premature publication — every persona flagged the unrun payroll stratification check; big-market called it a market-size confound dressed up as a development finding
weakest piece by consensus — r=0.27 within-GM persistence with CI crossing zero, then names names anyway. Three of four personas called it irresponsible.

universal_complaints: GM ranking publishes named-and-shamed leaderboard while admitting the persistence statistic doesn't support individual attribution.
Multiple articles publish findings while explicitly flagging central confounds as unchecked (payroll stratification on International Pipeline, max_fv coverage on Edge Decomposition).
Every chart is receiver-side. No persona reads the site for buyer-only research; net-sellers and sellers in specific deals are reading inverted material.
V3 model calibration is invisible. Every downstream finding inherits it and no published piece audits it.
where_personas_agree: K-trajectory is the strongest finding on the site.
GM ranking should not have named individual GMs at that signal-to-noise level.
Seller-side framing is a category gap, not an omission.
Coaching staff and dev-infrastructure people drive much of what's attributed to 'GM' and 'org'.

where_personas_disagree.topic: Is 'money isn't the gap' a real finding?
where_personas_disagree.big_market_says: No — outcome variable is net-of-cost, which mechanically penalizes high-payroll acquirers. The confound encodes the conclusion.
where_personas_disagree.midmarket_and_oldschool_say: Accept the finding directionally; the per-GM correlation of −0.09 looks robust.
where_personas_disagree.resolution_needed: Rerun with gross outcome (not net-of-cost) restricted to comparable trade archetypes.

where_personas_disagree.topic: What's the most valuable next research direction?
where_personas_disagree.midmarket_says: Model calibration audit — every downstream finding inherits this.
where_personas_disagree.bigmarket_says: Playoff-leverage outcome variable — receiver-side dollar surplus is the wrong objective at $250M payroll.
where_personas_disagree.rebuild_says: Seller-side framing on every existing article.
where_personas_disagree.resolution_needed: All four are valid. Prioritize by which expands the market the fastest.

consolidated_research_priorities.title: V3 model calibration transparency
consolidated_research_priorities.why: Every downstream finding inherits the model's calibration. Without published CRPS, coverage, and residuals, sophisticated readers can't validate the chain.
consolidated_research_priorities.deliverable: A standing 'Model Diagnostics' page (not an article) updated each refresh

consolidated_research_priorities.title: Seller-side companion to every existing article
consolidated_research_priorities.why: Every existing chart is receiver-POV. Sellers are inverting buyer research in their heads. The seller-side framing is often the more valuable side of the same data.
consolidated_research_priorities.deliverable: Series — 'The K-Trajectory Sell Window,' 'Where Your Prospects Appreciate,' 'The GM Seller-Side Leaderboard (FV per WAR shipped)'

consolidated_research_priorities.title: Coaching and dev-staff continuity layer
consolidated_research_priorities.why: Pitching coach, hitting coordinator, and Latin American academy director identity likely drive much of what the GM-edge decomposition attributed to org dev fit. Public data exists; not used.
consolidated_research_priorities.deliverable: Article: 'The Pitching Coach Effect' using coaches table

consolidated_research_priorities.title: Playoff-leverage outcome variable
consolidated_research_priorities.why: $250M payrolls don't optimize regular-season dollar surplus. They optimize playoff probability × playoff revenue. The current model framework doesn't see contender-acquirer trades correctly.
consolidated_research_priorities.deliverable: Article + alternative V3 outcome variable: playoff-prob delta × revenue weight

consolidated_research_priorities.title: Rental vs multi-year acquisition stratification
consolidated_research_priorities.why: 60% of contender trade volume is rentals (<1.5 yrs control). Treating them identically to multi-year vet acquisitions is statistical malpractice. Different decision problem, different math.

consolidated_research_priorities.title: K-trajectory follow-up — interactions and sell-side identity
consolidated_research_priorities.why: The site's best finding has obvious follow-ups: Q1 buy-list conditional on Stuff+ / arsenal stability, and who is concentrating as the Q4 sell-side.

consolidated_research_priorities.title: Per-destination prospect appreciation/depreciation curves
consolidated_research_priorities.why: When a rebuilder ships a 50 FV prospect, the destination org's dev fit determines how much surplus they're leaving on the table. The mirror of the org-fit hitter laboratory finding but seller-side.
consolidated_research_priorities.deliverable: Article: 'Where Your Prospects Go to Win' using org dev features per destination

consolidated_research_priorities.title: Recompute Edge Decomposition restricted to prospect-included trades
consolidated_research_priorities.why: The 'prospects don't differentiate' finding is partly 'most trades have no FV-graded prospect.' Re-running on the subset of trades that DO include a graded prospect would honestly test the claim.
consolidated_research_priorities.deliverable: Update / corrigendum to gm-edge-decomposition, OR new piece

category_gaps_called_out: Medical / injury risk transfer in trades
No-trade clauses and player consent leverage

what_built_credibility: Holdout windows are clean (2010-2020 train, 2021-2024 test) and stated
D-26 threshold framing is unusual and rigorous
Methodology callouts explicitly name confounds (this is good — but undermined when articles publish anyway)
what_undermined_credibility: Publishing findings with central confounds explicitly flagged as unchecked
Named-and-shamed individual GMs at r=0.27 persistence
Receiver-side framing presented as default without acknowledgment
No model calibration page anywhere on the site

summary_for_editorial_board: The site has a credibility-rich-actionability-poor problem. The methodology is better than FanGraphs or The Athletic on the same topics, but four different GM archetypes converged on the same complaints: rankings without persistence, findings without confound checks, and receiver-only framing. The fix is not more articles — it is targeted articles addressing the eight priorities above, plus a standing model-diagnostics page that lets sophisticated readers audit the chain instead of trusting it on faith.
